# Termina bounded terminal input

Sources are copied from [Termina 0.4.0, revision 7be7389fd3509d508a66a7e887aa9935e037b801](https://github.com/helix-editor/termina/tree/7be7389fd3509d508a66a7e887aa9935e037b801), with the reviewed local patch `32a7a905ab1c72b51463a93e96852d957b1c8448`. `upstream.json` records the finite original inventory and SHA-256 hashes before that patch. The repository's existing LF normalization applies to the copied sources; original hashes refer to upstream bytes. All production sources, embedded tests, examples, benchmark, Windows documentation and the original manifest are retained; upstream CI, development-shell files and lockfile are omitted.

The local `Cargo.lock` is generated by Cargo for Maka's standalone vendor tests and Windows compilation checks. It is generated build metadata outside the original source inventory.

The original MIT and MPL texts are preserved. Maka uses the MIT alternative offered by the upstream README. Keep that README: it also contains the original Crossterm (Timon, 2019) and TermWiz (Wez Furlong, 2018) MIT notices.

The bounded local changes are:

- Preserve primary DA terminal type and numeric attributes in `Csi::PrimaryDeviceAttributes`, and decode strictly decimal, nonzero `CSI 6;height;width t` cell pixels using the existing window-response type.
- Let the embedding reader set a pending-byte limit; the default remains unlimited. Checks happen before each byte is retained, including bracketed-paste framing. Completed events in the same OS read do not accumulate against this limit.
- Bound incomplete `CSI ?` metadata to 256 bytes and 100 milliseconds, advancing deadlines through the existing Unix and Windows input sources even without more input. Numeric CSI key prefixes do not receive a fragment deadline. Input resource/timeout failures remain sticky and return through `Parser::parse` and the same reader; rejected tails are never replayed as keys. Existing malformed-sequence handling is otherwise retained.
- Parse identified [Kitty graphics replies](https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/graphics-protocol/) through that same reader. `Event::KittyGraphicsResponse` preserves decimal `i`, optional `I`/`p`, and exact success or printable ASCII error text. APC (`ESC _`) is now a protocol prefix, like the existing OSC/DCS prefixes, rather than Alt+underscore. Complete unknown or malformed APC strings are discarded through ST; replies with duplicate, unknown, missing, or invalid identifier fields do not produce an event. APC strings share the existing 256-byte/100-millisecond sticky input-error bounds, so truncated or oversized strings cannot replay their tails as keys. These are local input resource limits, not protocol limits.
- Decode the existing mode-1016 DECRPM type and text-area pixel-size reports (`CSI 4;height;width t`) without selecting a rendering backend. SGR mouse reports use `Event::SgrMouse` with original signed coordinates: the application owns whether it enabled one-based cells or pixels. Kitty and Ghostty send zero-based pixels, including negative positions outside the viewport. Legacy mouse events retain zero-based cells. Kitty's bit-8 leave extension produces a coordinate-free `Event::MouseLeave`; all other button bits and coordinate values have no semantic effect on that event. No parser-side mode mirror is added.
- Enter Unix raw mode without flushing queued input. Allow Windows embedding owners to disable the existing discard-input-on-drop policy before starting their reader. Original mode/codepage restoration remains in the same terminal owner.

The local tests cover split replies mixed with Unicode/mouse/paste, strict parameters, Kitty query/placement responses, malformed APC isolation with following keys, a complete 64KiB paste, per-sequence limits, sticky rejection and deadline handling without delaying ordinary numeric key prefixes. Examples, documentation and the benchmark handle the fallible parser API.

After patch `32a7a905ab1c72b51463a93e96852d957b1c8448`, Maka adds a Windows-only console-record regression for completed-key preservation, sticky budget errors and rejected-tail isolation.

Maka's terminal shell owns the single OS reader and terminal mode guard; its existing Output worker owns terminal writes. This package does not add another reader, writer or capability-selection framework. Applications match Kitty response identifiers to their own outstanding requests; a response reports protocol acceptance, not that pixels have reached the screen. Image transmission, capability selection, and placement ownership remain in the embedding application. No general APC command framework or iTerm2 support is added by this patch.
